quality.label: Quality
quality.purpose: Durability, accounting quality and balance-sheet resilience; no profitability levels are reused.
quality.sectorTreatment: Generic formula stays NOT_APPLICABLE for banks, insurance carriers and REITs; those three cohorts are measured by the separately versioned templates under industryTemplates. Insurance agents, brokers and services (SIC 6400-6411) are not carriers and use the generic formula.
quality.missingDataPolicy: Invalid or unavailable inputs are null, never zero; legitimate negative values remain valid; available weights may renormalize only within the factor and must be disclosed.
quality.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation; counts are not winsorized.
quality.pitRequirements: Use only filing observations with availableAt<=scoreCutoff; prefer acceptedAt, otherwise validated filedAt; later restatements remain invisible until their own availability.
quality.updateFrequency: Event-driven after accepted filing/materialized consumer update; nightly snapshot only when a dependency changed.
quality.interpretation: Higher means stronger accounting durability and balance-sheet resilience, not a recommendation.

growth.label: Growth
growth.purpose: Operating expansion and acceleration; changes rather than profitability levels.

components.input: diluted EPS CAGR; both endpoints positive
free cash flow CAGR; both endpoints positive
current revenue YoY growth-previous revenue YoY growth

growth.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; no invented classification.
growth.missingDataPolicy: Cross-zero EPS or FCF CAGR is null; invalid inputs are never zero; within-factor renormalization is disclosed.
growth.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation.
growth.pitRequirements: All endpoints must have been available by scoreCutoff; use period identity and acceptedAt/filedAt lifecycle.
growth.updateFrequency: Event-driven after accepted filing/materialized consumer update.
growth.interpretation: Higher means stronger realized operating expansion, not expected revisions or a recommendation.

momentum.label: Momentum
momentum.purpose: Medium-horizon price strength and market confirmation on a split-adjusted price basis.

components.input: split-adjusted price return T-252 to T-21
security 12-1 split-adjusted price return minus certified broad benchmark 12-1 split-adjusted price return

momentum.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; no invented classification.
momentum.missingDataPolicy: Insufficient or semantically ambiguous price history is null; TOTAL_RETURN and SPLIT_ADJUSTED bases may not be aliased. Alle sechs Komponenten beruhen auf derselben splitbereinigten Kursbasis - eine gemischte Basis innerhalb des Faktors ist ausgeschlossen.
momentum.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after semantic validation.
momentum.pitRequirements: Use only final bars available before scoreCutoff and the certified benchmark observation aligned to each security date.
momentum.interpretation: Higher means stronger recent price confirmation, not a forecast, not a recommendation, and not the return an investor earned - dafuer steht investorReturn.
momentum.returnBasisWhy: Kursstaerke, nicht Anlegerrendite. Dividenden duerfen den Momentumrang nicht kuenstlich erhoehen; die Anlegerrendite steht als eigene Evidenz daneben (investorReturn).

value.label: Value
value.purpose: Price relative to current PIT-safe business fundamentals.
value.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; industry-specific applicability remains explicit. Banks, insurance carriers and REITs are measured by the separately versioned templates under industryTemplates instead of this generic formula.
value.missingDataPolicy: Negative earnings and FCF yields are valid adverse values; EV metrics require positive finite EV; negative equity makes bookToMarket unavailable.
value.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation.
value.pitRequirements: Price, shares, cash and debt must be the latest values known at scoreCutoff; no today-known values in historical scores.
value.updateFrequency: After completed EOD close or accepted filing when a dependency changed.
value.interpretation: Higher means cheaper relative valuation within the eligible universe, not intrinsic value certainty.

profitability.label: Profitability
profitability.purpose: Current and persistent operating profitability; excludes balance-sheet safety and accounting-quality components.

components.input: canonical return on invested capital; tax assumption disclosed

profitability.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; industry-specific applicability remains explicit. Banks, insurance carriers and REITs are measured by the separately versioned templates under industryTemplates instead of this generic formula.
profitability.missingDataPolicy: Negative margins and returns are valid adverse values; invalid denominators are null; within-factor renormalization is disclosed.
profitability.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation.
profitability.pitRequirements: Use only PIT-safe TTM and annual observations known at scoreCutoff.
profitability.updateFrequency: Event-driven after accepted filing/materialized consumer update.
profitability.interpretation: Higher means stronger current and persistent operating economics, not accounting quality or a recommendation.

revisions.label: Revisions
revisions.purpose: Changes in analyst expectations; SEC restatements and filing revisions are explicitly not this factor.

components.input: (current FY1 EPS consensus-prior consensus)/baseline share price
(current FY2 EPS consensus-prior consensus)/baseline share price
percentage change in FY1 revenue consensus
latest one-month FY1 EPS revision yield-preceding one-month yield
standard deviation of FY1 EPS estimates/share price

revisions.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; no invented classification.
revisions.missingDataPolicy: Without licensed immutable PIT consensus snapshots the entire factor is UNAVAILABLE; no proxy and no factor-weight redistribution.
revisions.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation; breadth is bounded and not winsorized.
revisions.pitRequirements: Same fiscal-period identity; actual provider publication timestamp; immutable current and baseline snapshots; corporate-action-adjusted per-share estimates; never reconstruct from today's history.
revisions.updateFrequency: Event-driven after a valid provider snapshot; nightly score snapshot only when dependency changed.
revisions.interpretation: Higher means improving analyst expectations, not a restatement signal or recommendation.
revisions.blocker: No licensed, certified historical PIT analyst-consensus source is present.

risk.label: Risk
risk.purpose: Historical market risk; a higher score always means lower observed risk.

components.input: annualized volatility of negative daily returns

risk.sectorTreatment: Industry then sector then universe normalization; no invented classification.
risk.missingDataPolicy: Insufficient or unaligned return history is null, never zero; within-factor renormalization is disclosed.
risk.outlierHandling: Continuous inputs are winsorized at peer and universe 2nd/98th percentiles after validation.
risk.pitRequirements: Only final total-return bars available before scoreCutoff and an aligned certified benchmark may be used.
risk.interpretation: Higher means lower observed historical market risk, not safety or a forecast.

requirements: product-eligible active US common equity or accepted ADR

classificationBinding.note: SEC SIC Division is an official SIC division, not GICS or a modern sector taxonomy.

normalization.unknownClassificationPolicy: Do not invent a classification; use documented universe fallback only when its minimum size is met.

score.quantScore: deterministic percentile rank of compositeScore in eligible score universe
score.semantics: Relative rank, not a probability, target price or recommendation.

temporal.currentMaterialization: nightly only if a dependency changed
temporal.canonicalHistory: immutable weekly snapshot using the final completed session
temporal.eventSnapshots: optional after material filing or large valid revision; never replace weekly history

valuationSemantics.statement: Every valuation component of this methodology divides an ISSUER-level figure (stockholders equity, net income, operating cash flow, dividends paid) by a market capitalization. The capitalization must therefore describe the same issuer, computed from the issuer's own share count and the price of the issuer's equity.
valuationSemantics.listingLevelRequires: A capitalization for one listed line requires a share count for that line. The SEC reports share counts per class on the filing cover page under the class axis; the bulk companyfacts dataset this house reads carries only undimensioned facts, so a class-level count is absent by construction, not by oversight.

measuredEvidence.whatTheDatasetShows: Alphabet and AT&T publish a current undimensioned TOTAL (12,230 and 6,852 million shares). Berkshire Hathaway's only observation is 1 million shares from 2011-03-31 and Accenture's is from 2010-02-28 - both pre-dimensional, both unusable. That is the signature of a dataset that drops dimensioned facts.
measuredEvidence.whyNoListingCanBeIdentified: No local source distinguishes a common share from a preferred, a note or an ETN. Measured over the 7,803 instruments of the security master: assetType is 'Stock' for 7,801 including FNGU (a leveraged ETN) and AMJB (a note); instrumentType is COMMON_STOCK for every one of them; CUSIP, FIGI and ISIN are absent for all 7,803; the security master's name rules cannot fire because the only available name is the issuer's SEC name; and the SEC ticker directory returns the same company name for every line. A ticker-suffix rule without a separator is provably wrong on this very universe, because GOOGL would become a preferred series of GOOG.

valuationSemantics.multiClassCommon: For genuine multi-class common lines such as GOOG and GOOGL the issuer capitalization must not be published once per line: that states one company twice and double counts it in any aggregate. Until a class-level count exists, both lines withhold.
valuationSemantics.nonEquityListings: A preferred share, a baby bond, a note, an ETN, a warrant or a unit is not a claim on the issuer's common equity and must never inherit an equity valuation from the issuer's fundamentals, whatever the security master's type field claims.
valuationSemantics.whatWouldChangeThis: A class-level share count. The cover-page tag is filed per class; recovering it needs the dimensioned facts, which is extraction work inside the existing SEC layer against the existing source - no provider purchase and no new pipeline.

knownDefectNotRepairableHere.what: The exported shares_outstanding series mixes concepts across periods without recording which concept produced which value.
knownDefectNotRepairableHere.evidence: JPMorgan alternates quarter by quarter between roughly 2,700 million and exactly 4,105,933,895, and the larger figure repeats bit-identically across nine fiscal years while the company's own per-share arithmetic implies 2,850 million. A real outstanding count drifts every quarter; a constant repeated for nine years is the issued count, which includes treasury stock. JPMorgan's price series carries no split, so nothing else explains the two levels.
knownDefectNotRepairableHere.scaleAndItsLimit: 228 published capitalizations deviate by more than 5 percent from the issuer's own per-share arithmetic. That figure is an upper bound on the defect and not a count of it: a stock split raises the outstanding count while the historical diluted-average series stays pre-split, so a split looks exactly like a mixed concept from the outside. Booking Holdings was read as a 23-fold error here until its own numbers were checked - 751 million shares at a split-adjusted 163.95 USD is internally consistent, and its capitalization is right. Only JPMorgan is verified as mixing, by the repetition and the absence of a split.
rejectedRepairs: An exact-repetition detector falsely flags NVIDIA's rounded 24,300 million and catches nothing where the wrong value appears once.

A ratio threshold against the issuer's own diluted scale cannot separate three different causes that all look alike: a mixed concept, genuine dilution, and a stock split. Measured, 433 titles have a latest observation above 1.25x whose earlier observations are in band.

Walking back to the most recent consistent observation substitutes counts up to two years stale - ADXN from 2025-12-31 to 2023-12-31, AGRO from 2025-12-31 to 2024-12-31 - and would undo a legitimate split.
knownDefectNotRepairableHere.correctFix: Record the source concept per value in the export and never mix concepts inside one metric series. That needs the raw facts, which are not in the repository.

industryTemplates.note: Separately versioned templates for the industries whose generic Quality, Value and Profitability formulas are NOT_APPLICABLE. Components are derived only from metrics the issuers already publish in the consumer fundamental export; nothing is substituted and nothing is renamed.
industryTemplates.normalization: Template components are normalized across the 974 titles inside the industry gate, with the peer leg narrowing to the SIC group as usual. The insurance-carrier range alone holds 130 titles and could never meet the contract's 200-issuer universe minimum; the shared cohort meets it for every component (minimum 436 valid issuers measured 2026-09-26).
industryTemplates.genericComponentsUnaffected: Generic components keep their population without the gated titles, so no previously published value changes. The extension only opens what was NOT_APPLICABLE.
industryTemplates.growth: Growth stays generic in this version. It is explicitly exempt from the industry gate and already AVAILABLE for 256 of 601 banks; replacing it would recompute existing values instead of opening closed ones. Measured consequence: 345 banks keep no growth factor because they publish no revenue series.

BALANCE_SHEET_FINANCIAL.label: Banks, savings institutions, lenders and brokers
BALANCE_SHEET_FINANCIAL.whyGenericFormulaFails: Gross profit, net debt and operating margin are not how a deposit-taking or lending balance sheet is measured; measured tag coverage in this cohort is gross_profit 15 %, operating_income 25 %, revenue 60 %, against total_assets 99 % and stockholders_equity 99 %.

INSURANCE_CARRIER.label: Insurance carriers
INSURANCE_CARRIER.notComputable: No combined ratio: incurred losses and underwriting expenses are not carried as separate tags in the consumer export, and a combined ratio without them would be one in name only.
INSURANCE_CARRIER.differsFromBalanceSheetFinancial: Carriers report revenue (premiums earned plus investment income) at 100 % measured coverage, so the margin on revenue is available to them and carries a quarter of the profitability weight.

REAL_ESTATE_TRUST.label: Real estate investment trusts
REAL_ESTATE_TRUST.notComputable: No FFO and no AFFO. Both require removing gains on property sales from earnings, and that position does not appear in the consumer export; measured, 89 % of these titles publish depreciation and none publish sale gains. The template therefore measures the operating cash flow and calls it that.
REAL_ESTATE_TRUST.whyEarningsCarryTheSmallestWeight: Depreciation dominates a property balance sheet, which is the very reason FFO exists. The earnings-based measure is kept for comparability but weighted lowest, and the cash measures lead.

mandatory: one of dividendCoverageByOcf, roaStability5y or positiveEarningsYears

knownGates: historical PIT universe membership and classifications

industry templates beyond banks, insurance carriers and REITs: a combined ratio for carriers needs incurred losses and underwriting expenses, an FFO for REITs needs gains on property sales, and neither position is carried in the export
an industry growth template: growth stays generic, so 345 banks without a revenue series keep no growth factor
broad component coverage and cross-sectional validation

versionHistory.change: Separately versioned industry templates for banks, savings institutions, lenders and brokers (SIC 6020-6220), insurance carriers (SIC 6300-6399) and REITs (SIC 6798) measure Quality, Value and Profitability where the generic formula is NOT_APPLICABLE. The insurance gate is narrowed from 6300-6411 to 6300-6399, so insurance agents, brokers and services use the generic formula. Growth stays generic.
versionHistory.why: 974 titles sat inside the industry gate and 2,922 factor cells said nothing but 'no industry template'. The cohorts publish the inputs their own industries are measured by - total assets and equity at 98-100 %, net income at 98-100 %, operating cash flow at 97-100 % - so the gap was a missing methodology, not missing data. No new source, no new provider, no renamed metric.

measuredImpact.reportingPeriodFilled: 4110 -> 4862 titles, +752 from the repair of the revenue-anchored period

versionHistory.whyTheEvidenceVersionDoesNotMove: vu-factor-evidence-2.0.0 keeps its snapshot series. The re-ranking is a side effect of returning 25 broker titles to the generic cross-section, and it was measured against every published record: mean 0.029 points, maximum 1.71, and not a single one of the 6,441 titles changes its change statement, because the change engine calls a factor move material at 3 points. Starting a new series would have emptied every title's comparison history to record a movement the engine itself does not consider one.

versionHistory.change: Momentum rechnet auf SPLIT_ADJUSTED_PRICE statt auf TOTAL_RETURN. Die Gesamtrendite wird als eigene Anlegerevidenz daneben gefuehrt und ist nicht mehr Bestandteil des Faktors.
versionHistory.why: Der Momentumfaktor misst Kursstaerke, Trenddynamik und Marktbestaetigung. Eine Dividende ist keine Kursbewegung und darf den Momentumrang nicht heben. Owner-Entscheidung vom 2026-09-24 (Option C) auf Grundlage der Full-Universe-Studie ueber 6.874 Titel und fuenf Stichtage.
versionHistory.previousBasisMeasuredNotAssumed: Alle 6.403 Eintraege von vu-factor-evidence-1.0.0 rechneten auf adjustedClose, und diese Spalte ist ueber 62.859 Dividendenereignisse als gesamtrenditebereinigt belegt. Die alte Bedeutung ist damit dokumentiert und laeuft nicht unter der neuen Version weiter.
